Annotators measured correctness (F‑score of finding labels), fluency (5‑point Likert scale), and content order (normalized Damerau‑Levenshtein distance).

We used three human evaluation metrics for the JLiverCT dataset: correctness, fluency, and content order metrics. Only correctness and fluency are used for the MIMIC-CXR dataset because of the time series irrelevant scenario. Correctness measures how well a report describes its clinical information. The fluency score evaluates the naturalness of the generated reports with a 5-point Likert scale. Annotators extract the positions of descriptions regarding any finding labels in the gold report and the generated report; then, these positions are used to calculate the normalized Damerau-Levenshtein Distance to obtain the content order score.
